title: Projected landscape and habitat dynamics for Malania oleifera (Santalales: Olacaceae) under climate change
content:
Abstract
Malania oleifera is an endemic endangered tree species. The effects of future climate change on the distribution pattern of suitable habitat for M. oleifera and its degree of fragmentation are unclear. The aim of this research was to investigate the impact of future climate change on the distribution and fragmentation of M. oleifera and to provide insights into conservation strategies for M. oleifera in China. The results showed that the distribution of M. oleifera is influenced primarily by precipitation in the driest quarter, isothermality, and mean ultraviolet-B of the lowest month. Areas of high suitability for M. oleifera are concentrated in Guangnan and Funing counties of Yunnan Province, alongside select counties in Guangxi and Guizhou provinces. It is worth noting that suitable habitats for M. oleifera are anticipated to diminish in the 2050s and 2070s. A reduction in the largest patch index and the patch cohesion index indicates that the areas suitable for M. oleifera are becoming less contiguous. An increase in the number of patches, patch density, landscape division, and the splitting index indicates that the landscape is becoming increasingly fragmented. Our study indicates that environmental factors are pivotal to the distribution of M. oleifera, with climate change posing significant threats to its habitat.
